issues.title: Asustor kernel drivers not loaded
issues.text: The fan and temperature readings and the front-panel LEDs need the asustor, asustor_it87 and asustor_gpio_it87 modules of the Asustor Platform Drivers plugin, built for the running Unraid kernel. After an Unraid update there may be no build yet: the page shows a red banner and Unraid one notification per boot. Wait for the build, or stay on the previous Unraid version.

issues.title: Front-panel LEDs have no driver
issues.text: Unraid's kernel has no leds-gpio or gpio-keys-polled driver, so the LEDs and the button the platform driver describes stay at their firmware state. The LED/button add-on on the LEDs and Buttons tab installs both for the kernels it has a build for.
issues.source: Unraid kernel configuration; asustor-platform-driver (leds-gpio and gpio-keys-polled platform devices)

issues.title: Bay order not confirmed
issues.text: Bay N is taken to be the Nth port of the ASM1166 SATA controller, as in the platform driver's LED table. Check it once with Locate on the LEDs and Buttons tab; correct the order there if a wrong tray blinks, and set Bay order confirmed.
issues.source: Enclosure profile of the plugin kit (asustor-as6706t)

issues.title: The CPU has no idle states (runs warm when idle)
issues.text: Linux found no CPU idle driver, so the cores only halt and the package never reaches its deep idle states: the CPU idles around 50 °C and the fan runs faster than it needs to. On these boards the firmware loads its C-state tables only when C-states are enabled in the BIOS setup. Enabling them there (a reboot into the BIOS setup) is the fix; owners of other Lockerstor units report much lower idle temperatures afterwards.
issues.source: /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpuidle/current_driver; Intel reference ACPI code (C-state tables loaded on demand); community reports (r/asustor, Lockerstor 4 Gen2)

issues.title: The SATA controller's PCIe link runs below what both ends can do
issues.text: The ASM1166 trained to a lower speed or fewer lanes than it and the board support. On a soldered-down controller this points at a fault of the board or its firmware; note it in a hardware report.
issues.source: PCIe link state from sysfs (current_link_* against max_link_* of both ends)

issues.title: PCIe errors counted on the SATA controller
issues.text: The controller counted PCIe errors since boot (AER). A few correctable errors are fixed by the link itself; a growing count belongs in a hardware report.
issues.source: AER counters from sysfs (aer_dev_correctable, aer_dev_nonfatal, aer_dev_fatal)

issues.title: A drive's SATA link runs below the port's speed
issues.text: A drive linked at a lower SATA speed than the port supports. Older drives link at 3.0 Gbps by design; for a 6 Gbps drive, reseat it in its tray.
issues.source: SATA link speed from sysfs (ata_link sata_spd against hw_sata_spd_limit)

firmware.text: No firmware version is read from the panel; the plugin only sends it text.
firmware.source: asustor-lcd (Asustor's LCD serial protocol, as documented by mafredri/lcm)
